learn.title: Angles in a triangle (recall)
learn.html:
The 3 angles of a triangle add up to 180°.

Equilateral: each angle 60°. Isosceles: 2 equal angles. Right triangle: the other 2 angles add up to 90°.

learn.title: Sum of interior angles
learn.html:
Cut a polygon into triangles from one corner. Each triangle gives 180°.

Quadrilateral (4 sides): 2 triangles → 360°
Pentagon (5): 3 triangles → 540°
Hexagon (6): 4 triangles → 720°
Octagon (8): 6 triangles → 1,080°

learn.title: Why a pentagon is 540°
learn.html:
From corner A, draw lines to C and D. The pentagon splits into 3 triangles.

3 × 180° = 540°

learn.title: Parallelograms and rhombuses
learn.html:
Angles between a pair of parallel sides add up to 180°.

Opposite angles are equal.

In a trapezium, the 2 angles between the parallel sides also add up to 180°.

learn.title: ABCD is a kite. Find ∠x.
learn.html:
A quadrilateral's angles add up to 360°.

∠x = 360° - 90° - 120° - 120° = 30°

learn.title: Angles at a point
learn.html:
Angles all the way round a point add up to 360°.

So a reflex angle (bigger than 180°) inside a shape = 360° - the angle outside.

questions.label: Do and Learn
questions.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. ∠DBC = 53° and ∠BCD = 108°. Find ∠ABD and ∠CDA.
questions.hint: Angles between a pair of parallel sides add up to 180°.
steps: AB and DC are parallel, so ∠ABC + ∠BCD = 180°. ∠ABC = 180° - 108° = 72°
AD and BC are parallel, so ∠CDA + ∠BCD = 180°. ∠CDA = 180° - 108° = 72°
questions.why: Angles between parallel sides add up to 180°.

questions.label: Exercise 1 (c)

questions.hint: The angles of a pentagon add up to 540°.
steps: The angles of a pentagon add up to 540°.

questions.why: 5 equal angles of 108°: 5 × 108° = 540°.

The angles of a pentagon add up to 540°. There are 3 right angles (at F, J and I): 3 × 90° = 270°.

questions.why: The key uses the hexagon's 120° angles and the 60° angle given at R.

questions.label: Exercise 3

steps: In the rhombus, triangle DFC has FD = FC, so ∠FDC = (180° - 110°) ÷ 2 = 35°
The rhombus is the same on both sides of DC, so ∠EDC = 35°

questions.why: The angles of triangle ACD: 23° + 105° + 52° = 180°.

questions.label: Exercise 5

∠DBE is a corner of the rectangle (90°): ∠DBC = 90° - 35° = 55°
questions.why: 35° + 55° = 90°, the rectangle's corner.

questions.label: Exercise 6

questions.why: The 5 point angles of this star add up to 180°: 30° + 40° + 25° + 45° + 40° = 180°.

learn.title: Perimeter of a polygon
learn.html:
The perimeter is the sum of all the side lengths.

Tip: tick each side as you add it, so you don't miss one or add one twice.

learn.title: Use multiplication for equal sides
learn.html:
Same tick marks = same length. Group them.

6 sides of 10.5 cm: 10.5 × 6 = 63 cm. Much faster than adding 6 times!

learn.title: Difference between 2 perimeters
learn.html:
Polygon A = 131.8 m, Polygon B = 124.8 m.

Difference = 131.8 - 124.8 = 7 m

learn.title: Split it into shapes you know
learn.html:
Cut the polygon into rectangles, squares, triangles and trapeziums.

Find each area, then add them.

Area of trapezium = ½ × height × (sum of the parallel sides)

learn.title: Equal pieces
learn.html:
A regular octagon splits into 8 equal triangles from the middle.

Find one triangle, then × 8.

learn.title: Octagon: 8 triangles of base 2.2 m, height 4 m
learn.html:
One triangle = ½ × 2.2 × 4 = 4.4 m²

Octagon = 4.4 × 8 = 35.2 m²

learn.title: Take away
learn.html: Sometimes it's easier to find a big rectangle and subtract the parts that are not shaded.

steps: Triangle A: base 5 m, height 4 m. Area = ½ × 5 × 4 = 10 m²
Rectangle B: 6 m by 5 m. Area = 6 × 5 = 30 m²
Square C: 6 m by 6 m. Area = 6 × 6 = 36 m²

The 2 thin triangles each have base 2 cm and height 8 cm: ½ × 2 × 8 = 8 cm² each

learn.title: Read, draw, solve
learn.html:
1. Read the problem twice.
2. Draw or look at the shape and write the numbers on it.
3. Perimeter → add the sides. Area → split into shapes.
4. Write the unit!

learn.title: A hexagonal tray
learn.html:
The perimeter of a regular hexagonal tray is 144 cm. Each side?

6 equal sides share 144 cm: 144 ÷ 6 = 24 cm

learn.title: Fencing an octagon
learn.html:
Emma's octagon playground has sides of 6.25 m. Fence length?

6.25 × 8 = 50 m

learn.title: Working backward
learn.html:
If you know an area, you can find a length.

Square of 144 m²: 12 × 12 = 144, so the side is 12 m.

Triangle of 16 m² with base 8 m: ½ × 8 × height = 16, so 4 × height = 16 and height = 4 m.

learn.title: Garden in 3 parts
learn.html:
① triangle ½ × 8 × 9 = 36 m²
② rectangle 7 × 8.2 = 57.4 m²
③ rectangle 41 × 11.3 = 463.3 m²

Total = 556.7 m²

learn.title: 6 triangles make a hexagon
learn.html:
John has 6 acrylic sheets in the shapes of equilateral triangles. Each side of each triangle is 12 cm long with the height of 10.4 cm. If he made a hexagon out of these triangles, find the perimeter and area of this hexagon.

The book says 10 cm, but the picture and the working use 10.4 cm.

Perimeter: the hexagon has 6 outside sides of 12 cm. 12 × 6 = 72 cm

Area of 1 triangle: ½ × 12 × 10.4 = 62.4 cm²
Area of 6 triangles: 62.4 × 6 = 374.4 cm²

questions.label: Exercise 5
questions.q: A wire 150 cm long is bent to form 4 equilateral triangles as shown below. Triangles ABC and ACG have the same area. Triangles CDE and CEF have the same area. Find the length of ABCFE.
questions.hint: Count how many long sides and how many short sides use up the 150 cm.

The small triangles use 5 short sides (CD, DE, EF, FC and CE).
So 5 sets of (long + short) = 150 cm. 1 set = 150 ÷ 5 = 30 cm.
ABCFE = AB + BC + CF + FE = 2 long + 2 short = 2 sets = 2 × 30 = 60 cm
questions.why: ABCFE uses 2 long and 2 short sides.

learn.title: Unit 10 big ideas
learn.html:
Angles: triangle 180°, quadrilateral 360°, pentagon 540°, hexagon 720°, octagon 1,080°.

Perimeter: add all sides (use × for equal sides).

Area: split into shapes you know.

learn.title: Check the height
learn.html: The height of a triangle meets the base at a right angle. A slanted side is not the height.

questions.label: Let's Think Along
questions.q: In the figure, ABCE is a rhombus and CDE is an equilateral triangle. ∠EAB = 80°. Find ∠EBD.
questions.hint: Find ∠DBC and ∠ABE first. Then use the angles in triangle ABC... along the straight edge.
steps: Opposite angles of a rhombus are equal: ∠BCE = 80°
BC = CE = CD, so triangle BCD is isosceles: ∠DBC = (180° - 140°) ÷ 2 = 20°

questions.label: Problem Solving
questions.q: Find the perimeter and area of the following figure.
questions.hint: It is made of 4 trapeziums, 2 squares and 1 rectangle. Use the tick marks for the perimeter.
steps: Perimeter: there are 8 slanted sides of 2.9 m and 14 sides of 2 m.
Area: 4 trapeziums ①③⑤⑦, each ½ × 2 × (2 + 6) = 8 m², so 4 × 8 = 32 m²
2 squares ②④, each 2 × 2 = 4 m², so 8 m²
questions.why: The figure is 22 sides long all round and made of 7 simple shapes.

questions.label: Math Journal
questions.q: Janice was finding the area of this polygon and got 224 cm². Do you think the solution done by Janice is correct? If not, in what part is not correct? Then correct it.
questions.hint: Look at the triangle on top. Which number is its height?
steps: Janice used 5 cm for the triangle's height. But 5 cm is the slanted side!
The real height is the dashed line: 4 cm.
questions.answer: No. She used the wrong height for the triangle. The correct area is 221 cm².
questions.why: The height must meet the base at a right angle.
